clue.text: One for sorrow, two for joy? Quite the opposite

definitions.text: One for sorrow, two for joy? Quite the opposite

blocks.clueFragment: One for sorrow, two for joy?
blocks.note: surface reading: the magpie rhyme, where one bird means bad luck and two mean happiness
setter's reading: count the spoken beats instead, and joy has one while sorrow has two

explanation.surface: Someone recites the old magpie-counting rhyme and is told they have it backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme sends you to magpies, but the numbers are counts of spoken units: JOY has one, SOR-ROW has two, so a SYLLABLE is what is being counted.
explanation.definitionFit: A syllable is a single unit of pronunciation, and the clue numbers how many of these each word contains.

clue.text: Settle up for waffle

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is written from bottom to top

blocks.note: to settle a bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: A plea to pay the bill instead of chattering on.
explanation.definitionFit: To yap is to talk at length about nothing much, which is exactly what waffling means as a verb.

clue.text: Freeloader in shelter next to church

blocks.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A scrounger dossing down in a shelter beside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is figuratively a person who clings to others and lives off them, a parasite or sponger.

clue.text: Wild colt I broke becomes servile type

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so the following letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written: all ten letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A horse-breaker tames an unruly young horse until it is fawning and obedient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' reads as the trainer's verb for taming a horse, but it is just part of the letters being mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bootlicker is someone who flatters and obeys superiors abjectly, a toady or sycophant.

clue.text: After slip, worker becomes wayward

blocks.note: to err is to make a slip or mistake
the worker ant: in crosswords a worker is very often ANT or BEE

explanation.surface: An employee goes off the rails after one mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means straying from the proper course, erring in conduct, which matches wayward behaviour.

clue.text: Gold ordered for morning delivery?

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
bade is a past tense of bid, meaning commanded

explanation.surface: Gold bullion ordered for a morning delivery, like a courier job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the past tense of bid. The 'delivery' is a performance, not a parcel.
explanation.definitionFit: An aubade is a song or poem greeting the dawn, so it is literally something performed in the morning.

clue.text: Opening of any new unit supplies another opening

indicators.note: the opening of a word is where it starts, so each of the next words gives its initial

blocks.note: first letter of any
first letter of new
first letter of unit
first letter of supplies

explanation.surface: Opening a new business unit leads to yet another opening, like a chain expanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' does double duty in the surface: first as the selector, then in the definition as a bodily aperture.
explanation.definitionFit: The anus is the body's rear aperture, an anatomical opening at the end of the gut.

clue.text: Poor working surroundings for money maker’s game

indicators.note: surroundings enclose something, so the first pair of words wraps around the next idea

blocks.note: poor quality is bad
a machine that is working is on
the Mint is where coins are made

explanation.surface: Grim working conditions for whoever earns the cash in some enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mint is the official factory that strikes a nation's coins, hence 'money maker'; the first two pieces are joined and then wrap around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket sport played with a shuttlecock over a high net, so it is a game.

clue.text: Basic requirement for successful parachute jump

definitions.note: a phrase describing what must happen, not a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: plain, practical and unpretentious
second meaning, taken literally: the jumper must come down to the ground

explanation.surface: A note on the fundamental rule for a skydive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basic requirement' reads as one phrase, but the clue splits after 'Basic'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone down-to-earth is practical and unpretentious, the plain basic sort; and literally a parachutist must reach the ground.

clue.text: It measures your velocity – during swim?

definitions.note: describes the swimwear by when it is worn

blocks.note: first meaning: colloquial short form of the dial on a dashboard
second meaning: a brand of swimwear, worn while swimming

explanation.surface: A question about whether a gadget tracks your pace while you are in the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: Speedo is a well-known brand of tight swimming trunks; speedo is also slang for a speedometer.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form names the gauge showing a vehicle's speed, and the brand name names swimming trunks.

clue.text: At sea, Tudor won second phase of fight

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters that follow are muddled

blocks.note: taken as written, eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A Tudor naval victory, the second stage of some war at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tudor navy fighting at sea makes 'At sea' look like scene-setting, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In boxing, bouts are split into numbered rounds, so the second one is the next stage of the contest.

clue.text: It’s at risk when making phone call

definitions.note: describes a situation rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: in jeopardy, as with a job or reputation
second meaning: connected on the telephone

explanation.surface: A warning that something is endangered whenever you pick up the phone, perhaps through hacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something staked is in jeopardy, ready to be lost; and a caller is connected on the telephone wire.

clue.text: Contemplating part of church windows, learner climbs up

indicators.note: climbing up means leaving one's place and moving higher, which in a down entry is earlier in the word

blocks.note: the nave is the main body of a church
glazing is the glass panes of windows
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plates; this is the letter that moves

explanation.surface: Someone gazing at a church's windows while a novice clambers up them.
explanation.walkthrough: No new L is added: the one already in the windows word lifts out and moves higher up the column, a movement rather than a plain charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Navel-gazing is self-absorbed reflection, literally staring at one's belly button while thinking deeply.

clue.text: Latest figures include returned contributions

indicators.note: the opening words include the solution within their run of letters
returned means sent back, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: reading the phrase backwards, the five letters sit across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: The most recent figures account for donations that have come back.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell 'Latest figures' backwards: SERUGIFTSETAL, and GIFTS is in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Gifts are things given freely, and contributions to a charity or fund are donations of that kind.

clue.text: Engaged by chance, strove desperately to become besotted

indicators.note: something engaged by another is held or occupied by it, so one piece goes inside the other
acting desperately means flailing wildly, so the word next to it is scrambled

blocks.note: luck is chance
the six letters mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone who got engaged by happy accident tried hard to fall truly in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaged' suggests marriage, but here it means held inside: the shuffled letters sit between the L and the UCK.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovestruck describes someone overwhelmed by romantic infatuation, which is what besotted means.

clue.text: Caesar came by empty commune that’s in northern Italy

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase rather than a noun

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its contents, so only the first and last letters remain

blocks.note: Julius Caesar's boast was veni, vidi, vici: I came, I saw, I conquered
the outside letters of commune

explanation.surface: Julius Caesar arrives at a deserted village in the north of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: VENI is Latin for 'I came', the first word of Caesar's famous phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Venice is a city on the lagoon in the Veneto region, in Italy's north-east.

clue.text: Retracted study about pests? Not to worry

indicators.note: retracted means drawn back, so the word is written in the opposite direction
about means around, so the first piece goes round the second

blocks.note: a den is a private room for work, a study
vermin are pests such as rats and mice

explanation.surface: Someone takes back a report about pests, telling everyone there is nothing to fear.
explanation.walkthrough: A den is a small private room for reading or work, which is why it can stand for a study.
explanation.definitionFit: Never mind is an idiom telling someone to forget about it and not be troubled.

clue.text: It has neck and defines it perhaps

definitions.note: a description: the word is a slang synonym for neck

blocks.note: first meaning: a glass container with a narrow top
second meaning: British slang for nerve, which can define neck in its sense of cheek

explanation.surface: A riddle about a thing that has nerve and also describes nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottle literally has a neck; and in British slang bottle means courage or nerve, as does neck (cheek).
explanation.definitionFit: A glass container narrows to a neck at the top, and the slang sense of nerve matches neck as boldness.

clue.text: Stretches out to take on regular heavy duties

indicators.note: to take on is to admit or accept, so one piece is received inside another
regular means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: someone stretched out lies down
second and fourth letters of heavy

explanation.surface: Someone sprawls out to take on hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duties' here means taxes, not tasks, despite the talk of heavy work.
explanation.definitionFit: Levies are taxes or charges imposed by authority, and duties are taxes on goods.

clue.text: Some money to be made from talking about meaning

indicators.note: talking about something means saying it out loud, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: tenor is the general drift or meaning of something said

explanation.surface: Money to be earned from giving talks about the meaning of things.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is an informal name for a ten-pound note, which is a sum of cash.

clue.text: Excessive deposit in heart may induce sweating there

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase rather than a noun

indicators.note: to deposit something in a place is to put it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the hub is the centre or heart of something
OTT is short for over the top

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding warning that fatty build-up in the heart may cause sweats.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT is the standard short form of 'over the top'. The surface reads like a heart-health warning, but 'there' points to a place to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot tub is a heated outdoor bath, a place to sit in hot water until you perspire.

clue.text: Chap whose happiness sets the standard for us all

definitions.text: Chap whose happiness sets the standard for us all

blocks.clueFragment: Chap whose happiness sets the standard
blocks.note: surface reading: a cheerful man everyone should model themselves on
setter's reading: the man in the British idiom comparing contented people to him, as happy as he is

explanation.surface: A man so cheerful that everyone else measures their happiness against him.
explanation.walkthrough: The British saying 'happy as Larry' means extremely happy, so this Larry is the benchmark of contentment.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names one fellow as the standard of great contentment that anyone else is compared with.

clue.text: Keep close tabs initially for a couple of weeks

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word before is used

blocks.note: a keep is the stronghold tower of a castle, a fort
nigh means near or close
first letter of tabs

explanation.surface: Advice to monitor someone closely from the outset over a two-week stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keep close tabs' reads as one phrase meaning watch carefully, but each word does a separate job.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortnight is a period of fourteen nights, which is two weeks.

clue.text: Setter’s pelvis broken in half by force

indicators.note: breaking something in half leaves only one half, so the back half of the word is dropped

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as I, so setter's (setter is) gives I'M
taken as written before cutting

explanation.surface: A crossword setter laments a pelvis broken by violence.
explanation.walkthrough: Pelvis has six letters, so half of it is the first three, PEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or push someone forward, to compel or force them into action.

clue.text: Deplore Republican vulgarian

blocks.note: to boo is to express disapproval loudly
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Someone decries a crude Republican politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A boor is a rude, ill-mannered person, and a vulgarian is a coarse person lacking refinement.

clue.text: Model has relations banned – don’t get involved

blocks.note: an artist's model sits for a portrait
it is an old euphemism for sex, so sexual relations
something banned is ruled out

explanation.surface: A fashion model has had their family relationships forbidden, with advice to keep clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' looks like family, but it means sexual relations, which crosswords often write as IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit it out is to stay on the sidelines and not take part, as an idiom for abstaining.

clue.text: Evaluate what to do after vacation

definitions.note: describes an action rather than a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: to analyse an idea by breaking it into parts
second meaning: to empty a suitcase on getting home

explanation.surface: Weighing up the post-holiday chores.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpack a concept is to analyse it closely, and to unpack luggage is to empty it on return from a trip.

clue.text: Refuse to acknowledge reduced reward

definitions.note: two senses here: reduced, and a share as reward

blocks.note: first meaning: to ignore someone pointedly, snub them
second meaning: lowered, or a share of the takings

explanation.surface: Someone declines to recognise a smaller bonus than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: The word works three ways: to snub, made smaller, and one's share of the proceeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone dead is to snub them; a price can be cut, lowered; and one's cut is a portion of profits.

clue.text: Middle managers trading fabrics from major African city

indicators.note: the middle of each word is its centre, so only the central letters are kept

blocks.note: central two letters of an eight-letter word
central three letters of a seven-letter word
central letter of a seven-letter word

explanation.surface: Mid-level bosses dealing in textiles from a big city in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle managers' reads as one phrase, but 'Middle' applies to each of the three words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadir is a large port and resort on Morocco's Atlantic coast, in north-west Africa.

clue.text: Plastic has affect bordering polluted lake

indicators.note: a border runs round the edge of something, so the first piece surrounds the second
something polluted is spoilt and corrupted, so the next word's letters are disordered

blocks.note: to bite is to take effect, to have an impact
the four letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Plastic waste has an impact on the shore of a dirty lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the definition; the anagram signal is 'polluted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bakelite is an early synthetic resin, the first commercially made plastic, used for old telephones and radios.
